overview: The School Committee approved the $89.1 million FY27 budget and selected a heat pump system for the Roberts Elementary HVAC project. The body also updated the Medford High School educational plan and established new policies regarding the use of AI in grading and the superintendent's evaluation cycle.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: The committee convened in executive session to discuss non-union personnel contracts, teacher grievances, and collective bargaining strategy for SEIU 888.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved routine bills, payroll, budget transfers, and meeting minutes from June 1 and June 8, 2026.

items.title: Mustang Moment: Music and Athletics Recognitions
items.summary: The Middle School String Ensemble performed following their MICCA gold medal win, and the superintendent recognized spring athletic championship achievements.

items.title: FY27 Budget Update and Approval
items.summary: Approved a final balanced FY27 budget of $89,100,000, which closed an $833,398 variance through staff reductions in high school teaching and paraprofessional positions while restoring an art teacher and inclusion specialist.

items.title: Roberts Elementary School HVAC Project Update
items.summary: Approved 'Option 1' (Air to Water Source Heat Pumps) for the school's HVAC and roof replacement project, citing its cost-effectiveness, compatibility with existing infrastructure, and minimal educational disruption. The project is partially funded through the MSBA Accelerated Repair Program.

items.title: Medford Public Schools Handbook Updates
items.summary: Approved handbook revisions that prohibit withholding recess as a disciplinary measure and establish a neutral academic honesty panel for student appeals.

items.title: MSBA High School Project Update
items.summary: Approved revisions to the educational plan and space summary for the high school project, reducing administrative office square footage to prioritize flexible innovation and performance spaces.

items.title: Space Alternative Study Resolution (2026-16)
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting the city share results of a study regarding the potential relocation of central administration and community services currently housed at the high school.

items.title: Student Travel Policy Update (2026-12)
items.summary: Approved updates to Policy JJH regarding student travel on second reading.

items.title: AI Guidance Policy (2026-14)
items.summary: Approved a policy amendment stipulating that educators should not use generative AI tools to provide feedback or assign grades to students.

items.title: Superintendent Evaluation Cycle (2026-15)
items.summary: Approved a resolution to align the superintendent's evaluation cycle with the school year, requiring goal presentations in September and final evaluations by June. The committee amended the resolution to require periodic progress reports.
